focus: Feedback loops in structuring: how late-stage decisions (goto count, condition extraction) feed back to earlier graph-modification stages, causing re-analysis of region identification and structural decisions. Key insight: SAILR and Phoenix use post-structuring metrics to drive edge-removal heuristics that re-trigger region identification and re-structuring cycles.

pipeline.name: AIL Conversion (Clinic)
pipeline.description: Convert function blocks to AIL blocks via Clinic analysis. This generates the base graph with AIL statements and handles call sites, returns, SSA, and variable recovery.

pipeline.name: Graph Simplification Passes (Before Region ID)
pipeline.description: Run optimization passes with stage BEFORE_REGION_IDENTIFICATION. These modify the graph structure (remove nodes, edges, inline, etc.) without yet knowing the region hierarchy.
pipeline.outputs: Modified clinic.graph; if out_graph is not None, updates addr_to_blocks and addr_and_idx_to_blocks

pipeline.name: Region Identification (RegionIdentifier)
pipeline.description: Recursively identify single-entry regions (SESE subgraphs) in the control flow. Finds loops via DFS back-edges, refines loop bounds, merges nodes, and builds GraphRegion hierarchy. This is the foundational step for structuring.
pipeline.inputs: clinic.graph, condition_processor, force_loop_single_exit, refine_loops_with_single_successor, complete_successors flags
pipeline.outputs: RegionIdentifier.region: GraphRegion (tree of nested regions); regions_by_block_addrs; loop_headers

pipeline.name: Region Simplification Passes (During Region ID)
pipeline.description: Optimization passes with stage DURING_REGION_IDENTIFICATION. These can modify the graph and MUST be followed by re-identification if they change it. This is the key feedback loop trigger.
pipeline.inputs: clinic.graph, region_identifier from prior step, reaching_definitions
pipeline.outputs: Modified clinic.graph and RE-COMPUTED region_identifier (line 657 and 661 re-run _recover_regions if graph changed)

pipeline.name: Recursive Structuring (RecursiveStructurer + PhoenixStructurer/SAILRStructurer)
pipeline.description: Recursively structure each region in post-order DFS. For each leaf region, apply the chosen structurer (Phoenix or SAILR) to convert the region graph into a structured AST (SequenceNode, LoopNode, ConditionNode, etc.). Phoenix matches schemas in order: cyclic loops (while/do-while), then acyclic (sequence, ITE, switch). SAILR adds recursive structuring with edge virtualization.
pipeline.inputs: region_identifier.region (GraphRegion tree), condition_processor, structurer_cls (Phoenix or SAILR)
pipeline.outputs: Structured AST (BaseNode tree): SequenceNode with nested LoopNode, ConditionNode, SwitchCaseNode; virtualized_edges set

pipeline.name: Region Simplification (RegionSimplifier)
pipeline.description: Simplify the structured AST by removing empty nodes, folding one-use expressions, simplifying if/else, loops, switches, and folding gotos. Produces goto_manager with all remaining gotos as a QUALITY SIGNAL.
pipeline.outputs: Simplified seq_node, goto_manager with gotos collected from GotoSimplifier

pipeline.name: Post-Structuring Simplification Passes
pipeline.description: Optimization passes with stage AFTER_STRUCTURING. These modify the AST only (seq_node), not the graph. Can rewrite conditions, fold expressions, etc.

pipeline.name: Code Generation (CStructuredCodeGenerator)
pipeline.description: Traverse the simplified AST and emit C code. Handle variable naming, type casts, expression folding, position mapping for click-mapping, and instruction-to-code mapping.
pipeline.inputs: seq_node, variable_kb, function prototype, AIL graph for reference
pipeline.outputs: C source code text, posmap (position mapping), instr_map (instruction mapping), variable types

After each DURING_RI pass, if a.out_graph is truthy, line 657 re-executes RegionIdentifier._recover_regions(ail_graph) with update_graph=False, rebuilding regions from scratch on the modified graph.

feedback_loops.trigger: PhoenixStructurer._match_cyclic_schemas (line 279-277) detects matching cyclic patterns (while, do-while) and marks edges with 'cyclic_refinement_outgoing'=True. These edges are then virtualized (removed) in _refine_cyclic, changing graph structure.

After _analyze_cyclic matches patterns and removes edges (line 1010-1019 in _refine_cyclic_core), the next iteration of the while loop re-runs _analyze_acyclic (line 192) on the modified graph. If _refine_cyclic removes the loop entirely (has_cycle becomes False, line 217), the loop updates state and continues.

feedback_loops.trigger: During _match_acyclic_schemas (line 1294), if the graph is modified (nodes replaced, edges removed), a GraphChangedNotification exception is raised (line 59-63), which signals that schema matching must restart.

On catch (line 1277), it resets idx=0 and continues the while True loop (line 1262), re-running _match_acyclic_schemas from scratch.

feedback_loops.name: Edge Virtualization Heuristic Selection (SAILR)
feedback_loops.trigger: SAILR's _last_resort_refinement (inherited from Phoenix, lines 228-241) needs to choose which edges to virtualize (remove) to break cycles. SAILRStructurer._order_virtualizable_edges (sailr.py:41-123) ranks edges by heuristics: H1 (fewest siblings), H2 (most post-doms), H3 (goes to return).
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Within the current _analyze() call, the selected edge is removed, potentially changing graph structure and cycle-ness. The while loop in _analyze (line 191) then re-runs _analyze_cyclic or continues to next iteration based on new 'has_cycle' value.
feedback_loops.mechanism: Heuristic-driven ordering (not explicit loop, but implicit via the while loop structure). SAILR's choice of which edge to virtualize affects which cycle patterns can be matched next, creating implicit feedback through the graph structure.

feedback_loops.name: Goto Count as Quality Signal (Region Simplifier + Optimization Passes)
feedback_loops.trigger: RegionSimplifier produces seq_node with goto_manager.gotos collected. Post-structuring optimization passes can inspect goto_manager and seq_node to decide if further deoptimizations are needed (e.g., 'duplication reverter' passes).
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Optimization passes marked with AFTER_STRUCTURING can modify seq_node based on goto count analysis. However, if a pass decides that the structure is unsatisfactory, it theoretically could feed back to earlier stages (though this is NOT currently implemented explicitly).
feedback_loops.mechanism: Implicit feedback through optimization passes. goto_manager is passed to post_structuring_simplification_passes (decompiler.py:452-458), which can inspect self.goto_manager and make decisions. SAILR's recursive design (recursive_structurer.py:56-123) allows sub-region structuring decisions to influence parent region handling.

feedback_loops.name: Condition Processor → Reaching Condition Recovery Iteration
feedback_loops.trigger: ConditionProcessor.recover_reaching_conditions() (condition_processor.py) extracts boolean conditions from AIL statements and uses claripy to simplify them. For complex regions, the simplification may reveal new structural patterns.
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Implicitly: if a condition simplification reveals that a previously matched schema was incorrect, the graph is modified, and region re-identification is triggered (via the Graph Modification → Region Re-identification Loop).
feedback_loops.mechanism: Not an explicit loop, but implicit through claripy-based condition simplification. When conditions are extracted (e.g., in region_identifier.py:609 _refine_loop_successors_to_guarded_successors), the simplified conditions may enable new structuring patterns in the structurer's _match_*_schemas() methods.

decision_points.name: Loop Single-Exit Enforcement
decision_points.decision: Whether to enforce single-exit loops via _refine_loop_successors_to_guarded_successors(). If force_loop_single_exit=True and region has multiple successors, convert to guarded successors using ConditionNode.
decision_points.alternatives: With force_loop_single_exit=True: multiple loop successors are converted to guarded branches. With False (SAILR mode): multiple successors allowed, affecting downstream structuring complexity.

decision_points.name: Loop Refinement Strategy
decision_points.decision: How aggressively to refine loop bounds. With refine_loops_with_single_successor=False, exit nodes are not included unless len(exit_nodes) <= 1. With True, more aggressive refinement including single-successor exit nodes.
decision_points.alternatives: Conservative (False, default for Phoenix): keep loop minimal, may produce multiple exit edges. Aggressive (True, optional for Phoenix): include single-successor nodes in loop, reducing exit count but potentially including more code.

decision_points.name: Complete Successors Mode
decision_points.decision: Whether to include successor nodes in graph_with_successors for cycle refinement. With complete_successors=True (SAILR), nodes reachable from loop exits are included.
decision_points.alternatives: With complete_successors=False: graph_with_successors may omit some successor nodes. With True (SAILR): more complete successor information for complex cycle refinement.
decision_points.anchor: decompiler.py:297-308 sets _complete_successors=True for PhoenixStructurer; passed to RegionIdentifier
decision_points.current_override: Set based on structurer_cls; passed to RegionIdentifier.complete_successors parameter

decision_points.name: Edge Virtualization Heuristic (SAILR)
decision_points.decision: Which edge(s) to virtualize (remove) when multiple exist. SAILRStructurer ranks by: H1 (fewest sibling in-edges), H2 (most post-dominators), H3 (goes to return).
decision_points.alternatives: H1 alone: minimal edge selection but may miss better choices. H1+H2: post-dom analysis (expensive) narrows to best edge. H1+H2+H3: return targets prioritized. H3 enables better duplication reversal later.
decision_points.current_override: SAILRStructurer._order_virtualizable_edges() uses all three heuristics in sequence; PhoenixStructurer._order_virtualizable_edges() uses simple address-based ordering

decision_points.name: Conditional Jump Rewriting to Break/Continue
decision_points.decision: When a loop is matched, which conditional jumps leaving the loop become 'break' vs which become 'continue'. Decision based on edge conditions (true vs false branch) and loop-back edge detection.
decision_points.alternatives: If wrong edge is chosen as 'back' edge: loop structure inverted. If continues/breaks mis-assigned: code semantics incorrect or generates extra gotos.
decision_points.current_override: Determined by _have_opposite_edge_conditions() check and edge condition recovery in condition_processor

decision_points.name: Switch-Case vs If-Else Decision
decision_points.decision: When acyclic schema matching, attempt switch-case detection before ITE. If a multi-way branch with address jumping is detected, treat as switch. Otherwise, if two-way conditional, treat as if-else.
decision_points.alternatives: If switch detection too aggressive: multi-case code mis-structured as nested if-else. If too conservative: switch not recognized, code unreadable.
decision_points.anchor: phoenix.py:1315-1330 (schema matching order: switch before ITE); 1345-1370 (_match_acyclic_switch_cases variants)
decision_points.current_override: Fixed schema order in _match_acyclic_schemas; switch matching has multiple strategies (memory-loaded addr, computed addr, incomplete head)

decision_points.name: Goto Simplification Depth
decision_points.decision: How many passes to run GotoSimplifier to remove unnecessary gotos. More passes catch more gotos but risk changing semantics.
decision_points.alternatives: Single pass: fast but may miss removable gotos. Multiple passes: thorough but slower. Affects final goto_manager content.

decision_points.name: Empty Node Removal Timing
decision_points.decision: When to remove nodes with no non-label statements. Early removal may prevent pattern matching; late removal may leave dangling nodes.
decision_points.alternatives: Remove before each optimization: cleaner intermediate state but may hide patterns. Remove once at end: simpler but intermediate states messier.

insights: Decompilers are NOT linear compilers: the angr decompiler has at least 3 major feedback loops that cause earlier stages to re-run. The key insight is that GraphChangedNotification exceptions (phoenix.py:59) and explicit re-identification calls (decompiler.py:657) serve as restart signals, allowing late-stage decisions (condition simplification, edge virtualization) to invalidate earlier region structures.

Goto count is a quality signal: The goto_manager collected during RegionSimplifier is not just diagnostic—it influences decisions in later optimization passes. SAILR's recursive structuring uses the current structuring state to decide whether sub-regions should be re-optimized. This creates an implicit feedback loop through the optimization pass pipeline.

Region identification is NOT just graph analysis: The RegionIdentifier uses heuristics (largest_successor_tree_outside_loop, force_loop_single_exit, refine_loops_with_single_successor) that embed choices about what constitutes a 'good' region. These choices are surfaced as parameters precisely because they affect downstream structuring success.

Phoenix schema matching is order-dependent but restarts on graph changes: The schema matching order (cyclic before acyclic, switch before ITE) is fixed, but GraphChangedNotification allows re-starting from scratch if a prior match modified the graph. This creates a subtle non-linearity: a switch match that removes nodes can invalidate a prior partial match on an acyclic ITE.

Condition simplification is a hidden rewind: ConditionProcessor.recover_reaching_conditions() uses claripy to simplify conditions. These simplified conditions are used in edge condition recovery, which affects which jumps are rewritten to breaks/continues. If simplification reveals new structure, it's implicitly captured by the graph-modification-triggered re-identification loop.

State is preserved across feedback loops: Unlike traditional compilers, angr preserves node_order, parent_map, and case_entry_to_switch_head across re-identification and re-structuring cycles. These persistent data structures allow decisions in one iteration to inform the next, creating true feedback rather than independent re-runs.

SAILR's post-dominance heuristic is computationally expensive but order-sensitive: H2 (post-dominator count) only runs if len(edges) <= postdom_max_edges and len(graph) <= postdom_max_graph_size. Hitting these limits silently downgrades to H1-only heuristic, creating a hidden decision point that affects edge removal order without explicit notification.

Virtualized edges accumulate knowledge: PhoenixStructurer.virtualized_edges (set of edges removed during cyclic refinement) is passed to recursion and affects how sub-regions are replaced in parents (recursive_structurer.py:122). This creates a persistent record of what was considered 'non-essential' for the current structuring, informing parent-level decisions.

Graph modification during structuring is not idempotent: The same region can be structured differently depending on whether certain optimization passes ran before. For example, an edge removed by StackCanarySimplifier may change which loops are detected by RegionIdentifier, changing the shape of the entire region hierarchy.

The base unit of scheduling is not 'a pass' but 'a graph state': Due to re-identification triggered by any DURING_RI pass that modifies the graph, the actual unit of work is a (graph, region_hierarchy, current_region) tuple. Two passes may nominally be at the same STAGE but execute in different effective stages depending on what prior passes changed.
